risks: Cross-plan order: step 1 needs flick-a513 step 1 (core::track Clock), step 2 (Cx.json replies) and step 6 (Event::Sleep/Locked/Unlocked); step 2 here needs flick-a513 step 5 (activity module with the `task` column). The epic is already blocked by flick-a513; do not start before those steps merge.

Event dispatch order: activity is registered before task, so on Started the task module posts TaskChanged with events::post (delivered on the next main-queue turn) rather than relying on order within one dispatch.

Double counting: activity and tasks both react to Idle/Active. They use the same core Clock rules, so a task's time and the activity spans tagged with it agree to within the 2 s flicker merge; a test feeds the same event script to both clocks and compares totals.
Main-thread borrow: TaskChanged arrives via events::post; app::on_event re-queues on contention (mulch mx-fcbc43). Handlers only update in-memory state and write one row.

Ambiguous titles from the CLI: prefix matching could start the wrong task. Mitigation: exact title wins, a non-unique prefix is an error listing the candidates, and ids always work; `--json` replies include ids.
Usage table growth: per-task root items would add a usage row per task forever. Mitigation: fixed root item ids; views use record_use = false.
Crash: the open task_time row's end advances on every event; at worst the time since the last event is lost. Same trade-off as activity.
check:size and coverage: keep files under 500 lines (store.rs, clock glue, cli.rs, views.rs); add a coverage floor for the pure parts (`src/modules/tasks/cli.rs` argument parsing and report shaping).
Table names must start with `task` (characterization store_schema, mulch mx-c65bc5).
ASSUMPTION: status is todo | doing | done; 'doing' means started at least once and not done; 'running' is separate (at most one task, with an open time row).
ASSUMPTION: task timing does not need activity recording on: starting a task is explicit consent to time it. Span attribution happens only while activity recording is on.
ASSUMPTION: `start <title>` creates the task when nothing matches, and in the launcher a trailing `#word` sets the project.
ASSUMPTION: report ranges are local days (platform::clock::utc_offset); a week is Monday to Sunday.
ASSUMPTION: no cmd+K action menu dependency; per-task actions are rows in a pushed view. When pl-39d2 lands, moving them to cmd+K is a separate follow-up.
acceptance: `scripts/check-all.sh` passes after every step; src/core/ stays at 100% line coverage; the module diff is src/modules/tasks/ plus one `modules!` line (plus Event::TaskChanged in core and the activity change in step 2).
`flick task start "Write plan" --project flick` creates and starts the task; `flick task ls` marks it running; `flick task stop` stops it; `flick task report` shows its time within 5 s of wall clock.
`flick --json task ls | jq .ok.running.id` and `flick --json task report today | jq .ok.total_secs` print numbers; without --json both print readable text.
Starting task B while A runs switches: A's row closes, B's opens, and `flick events` shows one `{"event":"task_changed","task":<B>}`.
Idle: with a task running, 2+ minutes without input end the task's time ~60 s after the last input; input resumes it. Locking the screen and sleeping pause it at once; unlock and wake resume it.
With activity recording on, `flick activity today --by task` shows time under the running task's id, and spans before the start and after the stop have no task.

Launcher: 'Start Task', typing 'Review PR #kota' and Enter creates and starts the task in project kota; 'Stop Task: Review PR · 0:03' appears while it runs; 'Tasks Today' lists today's totals per task and per project.
The running task survives `flick reload` and a Flick restart.
`flick task done <id>` stops and completes it; done tasks disappear from `ls` and the pick view but stay in reports.
Idle CPU ~0% over 60 s with a task running (no timers added).
Privacy: tasks live only in flick.db; the module has no network code (grep as in flick-a513).
Manual smoke: launcher, clipboard, switcher, window keys, desktop toggle and activity recording behave as before.

sections.context: I run coding agents (claude, pi, codex) in herdr 0.9.1 (/opt/homebrew/bin/herdr) on four machines: local (this MacBook Pro), mbp-server (always-on hub), mac-pro-jaymin and mac-pro-kota; the last three are saved SSH machines (`herdr machine list`). To see which agent waits on me I attach the herdr TUI and walk machines with prefix+w. Roots r-5052 (commit 87ac539): v1 only monitors and jumps; no replies, no chat UI. Flick should list agents on all machines with the ones waiting on me first and a preview of recent output, focus an agent's herdr pane on Enter, and optionally notify when an agent starts to wait. Findings from read-only inspection (herdr --help, --skill, `herdr api schema --json`, `herdr agent list`): (1) local server socket ~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock (mode 0600, $HERDR_SOCKET_PATH inside herdr panes), newline-delimited JSON requests `{"id","method","params"}` and replies `{"id","result"}`; (2) methods include agent.list, agent.get, agent.read (source recent-unwrapped, lines), agent.focus, session.snapshot, ping, events.subscribe and events.wait; (3) events.subscribe takes global subscriptions (pane.created, pane.closed, pane.exited, pane.updated, pane.agent_detected, ...) and per-pane `pane.agent_status_changed` (requires pane_id), and pushes `{"event":"pane_agent_status_changed","data":{pane_id,workspace_id,agent,agent_status,title,...}}`; (4) agent_status is idle | working | blocked | done | unknown; `blocked` means an approval or question UI, `done` means finished and not yet seen; AgentInfo carries pane_id, agent, name, cwd, terminal_title_stripped, focused, state_change_seq; (5) `--machine <label>` forwards one request/response command over SSH (~2.8 s per call to mbp-server); the schema has no machine field, so there is no forwarded event stream, and Flick must not implement SSH itself (seed). herdr-msg (the messaging hub) is unrelated and out of scope.
sections.approach:
Module `herdr` (src/modules/herdr/, registry line `mod herdr => "herdr", herdr::Herdr::default;` after the task/activity modules). No FFI in the module: local transport is std UnixStream, remote transport is the herdr CLI. Background threads own all I/O; they update shared state and post `Event::ModuleChanged { module: "herdr" }` (flick-9639, pl-5490 step 2), so the visible view refreshes. Five steps.

1. Pure fleet model (`src/modules/herdr/model.rs`, 100% coverage, serde with unknown fields ignored). `Agent { machine, pane_id, workspace_id, kind, name, status, cwd, title, focused, seq }` parsed from agent.list results; `Fleet { machines: BTreeMap<String, MachineState { agents, updated_at, error: Option<String> }> }` with `apply_list(machine, agents, now)`, `apply_event(machine, event)` (status change, pane closed/exited, agent detected), and `transitions()` returning agents that entered `blocked` or `done` from another state (for notifications). Ordering for display: blocked, then done, then idle, then working, then unknown; within a group the most recent `seq` first; machine order from config. `preview(text, lines)` keeps the last N non-empty lines with ANSI already stripped by herdr (strip_ansi true) and trims to 200 chars. Fixtures are synthesized from the 0.9.1 schema (no real terminal output committed).

2. Transport (`src/modules/herdr/local.rs`, `remote.rs`, no module wiring yet). Local: connect to `socket` (default ~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock), `ping` to check protocol (22 in 0.9.1; a different protocol logs a warning and still tries), `agent.list`, then one long-lived subscription connection with global subscriptions (pane.agent_detected, pane.closed, pane.exited, pane.created, pane.updated) plus `pane.agent_status_changed` for each agent pane, re-subscribing when panes appear (open a new subscription connection and drop the old one if a second events.subscribe on the same connection is rejected; the step records which works). On disconnect (herdr server not running), the thread stops and the module reconnects on the next LauncherOpened, view open or Wake, never in a retry loop. Requests `agent.read {target, source: recent-unwrapped, lines: 40}` and `agent.focus {target}`. Remote: run `<herdr> --machine <label> agent list|read|focus ...` with HERDR_* env removed (as herdr-msg does), 10 s timeout, stdout parsed as `{"id","result"}`, stderr JSON errors surfaced. Spike in this step (results go in the step's commit message and a mulch record): does `pane.updated` fire on agent status changes; does `herdr --machine X agent focus` make the local TUI client show that machine's pane; does any forwarded or client-socket path give a remote event stream in 0.9.1. Tests: a fake herdr server on a short Unix socket path (mulch mx-6c21fe: /tmp/fk.XXXX) and a fake `herdr` shell script for the CLI runner.

3. Platform notifications (`src/platform/notify.rs`): `notify::request_permission()`, `notify::post(id, title, body)` and a click handler `notify::on_click(fn(&str /*id*/))` over UNUserNotificationCenter with a delegate class (objc2 define_class!, fn-pointer handler per mulch mx-db09fc); a no-op returning Err when the process has no bundle identifier (cargo run), because UNUserNotificationCenter raises without one. Adds the objc2-user-notifications crate (check:deps, binary budget). Independent of herdr; any module can use it later.

4. Module `herdr`: config `[herdr]`: `herdr = "herdr"` (resolved on PATH, then /opt/homebrew/bin/herdr), `socket = "~/.config/herdr/herdr.sock"`, `machines = []` (empty: local plus every enabled machine from `herdr machine list --json`, read once on Started/reload), `remote_refresh_secs = 60` (0: remote machines refresh only when the view opens), `terminal = "WezTerm"` (app to bring to the front on jump), `hotkey = ""`, `notify = ["blocked"]` (subset of blocked, done; empty disables), `preview_lines = 6`. Root item 'Herdr Agents' with subtitle '2 waiting · 7 agents · 4 machines' (id `herdr:agents`; no per-agent root items, so the usage table never grows with ephemeral pane ids). View `herdr/agents` (record_use = false): one row per agent, title '<name or kind> · <machine>', subtitle '<status> · <cwd basename> · <last preview line>', ordered by the model; machine errors appear as a row ('mac-pro-kota: unreachable, 3 min ago'). Enter = jump: `agent.focus` (local socket or `--machine`), then open the terminal app (`workspace::open_file` on its .app path, existing platform API) after `cx.hide()`, return Outcome::Hide; if step 2's spike found the local client does not follow a remote focus, the status line says 'Focused on mbp-server; press prefix+w in herdr'. Tab = detail view `herdr/agent` listing the last `preview_lines` lines of `agent.read` (fetched in the background on open, held in memory only) with 'Jump' as the first row. Remote refresh: on view open and LauncherOpened (at most once per 15 s), plus every `remote_refresh_secs` on one background thread that sleeps between runs (no main-thread timer; a sleeping thread costs no CPU), machines in parallel. CLI: `flick herdr ls [--json]` (cached fleet, `--refresh` waits for a fresh read up to 10 s), `flick herdr jump <machine>/<pane_id|name>`, `flick herdr status` (per machine: connected/last refresh/error). Uses `cx.json` from flick-a513 step 2.

5. Notifications, docs and smoke. On `transitions()` for a status in `notify`, post `notify::post("<machine>/<pane>", "<name> is waiting", "<machine> · <cwd> · <title>")`, at most one per agent per state change, none for an agent herdr reports `focused` while the terminal app is frontmost; clicking the notification jumps to it (same path as Enter). README 'Herdr' section (what is read, nothing stored, `--machine` uses herdr's own SSH profiles), ARCHITECTURE note (module-owned I/O threads + ModuleChanged pattern, platform::notify), DEFAULT_CONFIG `[herdr]` example, manual checklist.

Parallelism: steps 1, 2 and 3 touch disjoint files and run at the same time. Step 4 needs 1 and 2 plus flick-9639 (pl-5490 step 2, Event::ModuleChanged) and flick-a513 step 2 (--json replies). Step 5 needs 3 and 4.

risks: Cross-plan dependencies: step 4 needs flick-9639 (pl-5490 step 2, Event::ModuleChanged) and flick-a513 step 2 (Cx.json replies). If ModuleChanged has not landed, do not add a second variant; wait or land flick-9639 first.

herdr API drift: herdr updates often (protocol 22 in 0.9.1). Mitigation: serde ignores unknown fields, enums fall back to Unknown, `ping` logs a protocol mismatch, and `flick herdr status` shows the server version. Only stable methods are used (agent.list/read/focus, events.subscribe, ping).

Remote latency and failure: `--machine` costs ~2.8 s per call and fails when a Mac sleeps (mac-pro-*). Mitigation: all remote calls on background threads, machines in parallel, 10 s timeout, cached rows with age and an error row; the launcher never waits on SSH.

Remote jump: `agent.focus` on a remote server may not switch the local TUI client to that machine. Step 2's spike decides; fallback is a status line telling me to press prefix+w. Flick never starts `herdr --remote` or a new terminal session.

Event stream gaps: per-pane `pane.agent_status_changed` needs a subscription per pane; if a new agent appears between list and subscribe, its first change is missed. Mitigation: subscribe to pane.agent_detected/pane.created globally and re-list on those; `seq` (state_change_seq) detects stale rows.

Idle CPU: the local subscription thread blocks in read (no timeouts, mulch mx-bd9f16); the remote refresh thread sleeps `remote_refresh_secs` between runs. Each remote refresh spawns 3 short herdr/ssh processes per minute; acceptance measures it.

Privacy: agent output previews can contain code and secrets. They stay in memory only (never in flick.db or logs), are fetched only when the detail view opens or for notification bodies (title/cwd only, no output in notifications).

Notifications need a bundle id and the user's permission; `cargo run` and an unsigned build have no bundle id. Mitigation: notify is a no-op returning Err there, and `flick herdr status` reports 'notifications: not permitted' when denied.

Main-thread borrow: worker threads never touch module state through the controller; they update an Arc<Mutex<Fleet>> and `events::post(ModuleChanged)`; on_event only reads the snapshot (mulch mx-fcbc43, mx-1d2d92).
Socket paths in tests exceed 104 bytes under $TMPDIR (mulch mx-6c21fe): use /tmp/fk.XXXX for the fake herdr server.

Environment leakage: when Flick is started from a herdr pane (dev runs), inherited HERDR_PANE_ID/HERDR_SOCKET_PATH would retarget commands. Mitigation: strip HERDR_* from the child env and use the configured socket path.
check:size and coverage: keep files under 500 lines (model.rs, local.rs, remote.rs, mod.rs, views.rs); add a 100% coverage floor for src/modules/herdr/model.rs.
Dead code: notify (step 3) is unused until step 5; use `#[cfg_attr(not(test), expect(dead_code, reason = "wired in flick-3cc9 step 5"))]` and remove it there.

ASSUMPTION: jump = herdr `agent.focus` on the agent's server, then bring the configured terminal app (default WezTerm, the only terminal installed) to the front.
ASSUMPTION: notifications default to `blocked` only (an approval or question waits on me); `done` is opt-in. Notification text holds name, machine, cwd and title, never terminal output.

ASSUMPTION: preview = last 6 non-empty lines of `agent.read --source recent-unwrapped --lines 40`, shown in a Tab detail view and as the last line in the row subtitle for local agents; remote previews load only when the detail view opens.

name: herdr: monitor agents across machines and jump to them

sections.context: Shottr (region/window capture to clipboard + file, quick annotation) and Presentify (draw on the screen, cursor highlight) are two more menu bar apps Flick can replace. Flick already has what the glue needs: a launcher with root items, views and action menus, module hotkeys, a control socket with structured --json replies (Cx.json), Event::ModuleChanged for background work (posted by the rebuild module), platform::pasteboard (text only today), workspace::open_file/reveal, files::trash, screens::visible_areas and a non-activating NSPanel pattern in platform::panel. Missing: a capture backend, an image pasteboard write, an annotation model and canvas, an editor window, a click-through screen overlay, and the capture module itself. Agents also benefit: `flick capture screen --json` gives a path an agent session (flick-3aac, later) can read.
sections.approach:
Module `capture` (src/modules/capture/, registry line `mod capture => "capture", capture::Capture::default;` after `rebuild`), plus two platform pieces: `platform::capture` (the shutter) and `platform::ink` (annotation model, canvas view, editor window, screen overlay). No new crates and no core changes. Seven steps; steps 1 and 2 run in parallel, step 5 runs beside 3 and 4.

Capture backend: `/usr/sbin/screencapture` driven from platform (same pattern as platform::hid driving hidutil). It gives the native area/window selection UI (crosshair, Space toggles window mode, Esc cancels, multi-display, Retina pixels, window shadows) with zero UI code and no binary growth. ScreenCaptureKit is kept as a later option (see alternatives).

1. Platform: `src/platform/capture.rs` (new, `pub mod capture;` in platform/mod.rs) and `src/platform/pasteboard.rs`. `pub enum Target { Area, Window, Screen /* display under the mouse */, Display(u32), Rect(Rect) }`, `pub struct Request { target, path: PathBuf, cursor: bool /* -C */, shadow: bool /* -o when false */, sound: bool /* -x when false */ }`, `pub fn args(&Request) -> Vec<String>` (pure: Area => -i, Window => -i -w, Display(n) => -D n, Rect => -R x,y,w,h, always -t png), `pub fn run(&Request) -> Result<Shot, Error>` (blocking; spawns screencapture, waits, returns `Shot { path, width, height }` read from the PNG IHDR; an interactive run that exits without a file is `Err(Cancelled)`), `pub fn png_size(&[u8]) -> Option<(u32, u32)>` (pure), `pub fn permitted() -> bool` (CGPreflightScreenCaptureAccess) and `pub fn request_permission() -> bool` (CGRequestScreenCaptureAccess), both FFI with SAFETY comments. `pasteboard::set_png(bytes: &[u8])` writes NSPasteboardTypePNG (and TIFF via NSBitmapImageRep for apps that only read TIFF). Tests: args table for every Target and flag; png_size on a fixture header, truncated and non-PNG input; `run` with Target::Display(1) into a temp file is `#[ignore]`d (needs Screen Recording) and documented as a manual smoke. Mark every pub item `#[cfg_attr(not(test), expect(dead_code, reason = "wired in flick-abc0 step 5"))]` (mx-2d069e).

2. Platform pure model: `src/platform/ink/mod.rs` (`pub mod ink;`, re-exports) and `src/platform/ink/model.rs` (plain Rust, no objc2). `Point`, `Color(u8 index into a palette)`, `Style { palette: Vec<[f32;4]>, width: f32, fade_secs: f32 }`, `Tool { Arrow, Rect, Pen, Highlight, Text, Redact }`, `Shape { tool, color, width, points: Vec<Point>, text: Option<String>, at: f64 }`, `Canvas { shapes, undone, drag }` with `begin(tool, color, p, now)`, `drag(p)` (pen/highlight append points more than 1 pt apart; arrow/rect/redact keep start and end), `end() -> bool` (a zero-size rect or arrow is dropped), `add_text(p, text)`, `undo()`, `redo()`, `clear()`, `expire(now, fade_secs) -> bool` (overlay fade), `arrow_head(from, to, width) -> [Point; 3]`, `normalized(a, b) -> Rect`, `scaled(&Shape, k) -> Shape` (points to pixels for export), and `key_command(chars: &str, cmd: bool, shift: bool) -> Option<Command>` (a/r/p/h/t/x pick tools, 1-5 colors, cmd+z undo, cmd+shift+z redo, Delete clears, Return done, cmd+c copy and done, cmd+s save, Esc cancel). Add `"src/platform/ink/model.rs": 100.0` to scripts/coverage-budgets.json. Unit tests cover every branch. dead_code expects cite step 3.

3. Platform canvas and editor: `src/platform/ink/view.rs` (define_class `FlickInkView`: NSView, flipped, draws the Canvas with NSBezierPath (arrows with filled heads, rect outlines, pen strokes with round joins, highlight at 35% alpha and 3x width, redact as a filled black rect, text with NSFont system 18 pt scaled by width), mouseDown/Dragged/Up feed the Canvas, keyDown maps through `key_command`, Text tool opens an NSTextField at the click and commits on Return; one `fn draw_shapes(&[Shape], scale)` shared by on-screen drawing and export) and `src/platform/ink/editor.rs`: `pub struct EditOpts { style: Style, copy: bool }`, `pub fn edit(src: &Path, dest: &Path, opts: EditOpts, on_done: fn(Done)) -> bool` with `enum Done { Saved, Copied, Cancelled }`. The editor is a titled NSWindow sized to the image in points (NSImage size from the PNG DPI), fitted to `screens::visible_areas()[0]`, centered, the image as background and FlickInkView on top. It activates Flick so keys work (Flick is an accessory app). Return or cmd+C flattens: NSBitmapImageRep at the image pixel size, draw image then `draw_shapes(scaled by pixels/points)`, write PNG to `dest`, `pasteboard::set_png` when `opts.copy` or cmd+C; cmd+S writes without copying; Esc or the close button calls `on_done(Cancelled)` and writes nothing. `on_done` runs on the main thread from an AppKit callback: callers must only `events::post` (mx-fcbc43). One editor at a time; a second `edit` brings the open one to front and returns false. Tests: what can run without a window (flatten math via model, option plumbing); the window itself is a manual smoke. Each file under 500 lines (mx-e7e3ab).

4. Platform overlay: `src/platform/ink/overlay.rs`. One borderless NSPanel per NSScreen (style Borderless | NonactivatingPanel, clear background, level above the menu bar and Dock (NSScreenSaverWindowLevel), collection CanJoinAllSpaces | Stationary | FullScreenAuxiliary | IgnoresCycle), each holding a FlickInkView with its own Canvas. API: `pub fn set_drawing(on: bool, style: &Style)` (on: panels accept mouse, become key without activating Flick, so Esc, 1-5, a/r/p/h, cmd+z work; off: `ignoresMouseEvents = true`, click-through), `pub fn drawing() -> bool`, `pub fn clear()`, `pub fn set_cursor(halo: Option<Halo { color, radius }>)` (a ring that follows the pointer and a click pulse, from NSEvent global and local monitors for mouseMoved/dragged/down, installed only while on; no timer), `pub fn relayout()` (rebuild panels after DisplaysChanged), and fade: when `style.fade_secs > 0`, one `timer::after` per finished stroke calls `Canvas::expire`. Esc while drawing turns drawing off and clears (Presentify behavior); panels are ordered out when neither drawing, strokes nor halo remain, so an idle overlay costs nothing. Shapes stay visible, click-through, after drawing ends until Esc or `clear()`. dead_code expects cite step 6.

5. Module `capture` without ink (needs step 1). Files: `src/modules/capture/mod.rs` (Module impl), `store.rs` (migration 1: `capture_shots(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, path TEXT NOT NULL, kind TEXT NOT NULL, width INTEGER NOT NULL, height INTEGER NOT NULL, taken INTEGER NOT NULL)` with an index on `taken`; extension trait `Shots` per mx-0f419d; cap rows at `history` (default 200) without touching files), `name.rs` (pure: file name from a template, default `Flick {date} at {time}.png` with local time from `clock::utc_offset` and `core::track::local_day` (or its own civil-date helper), ` (2)` suffix on collision, `~` expansion), `run.rs` (async shot: `Arc<Mutex<Vec<Result<Shot, Error>>>>` filled by a worker thread that calls `capture::run`, then `events::post(Event::ModuleChanged { module: "capture" })`, following the rebuild module's background-thread pattern). Config `[capture]`: `dir = "~/Pictures/Flick"` (created on first save), `name`, `copy = true`, `save = true` (false: temp file, clipboard only, not recorded), `sound = true`, `cursor = false`, `shadow = true`, `history = 200`, `area_hotkey`, `window_hotkey`, `screen_hotkey` (all empty by default). Root items: `capture:area` Capture Area, `capture:window` Capture Window, `capture:screen` Capture Screen, `capture:recent` Recent Captures (pushes view `capture/recent`). Activate: check `capture::permitted()` first (else `request_permission()` and `Stay(Some("Allow Screen Recording for Flick in System Settings"))`), `cx.hide()`, start the worker, return Hide. On ModuleChanged: drain results, `pasteboard::set_png` when copy, insert the row, return true (stale recent view). View `capture/recent`: rows `capture:shot/<id>` (file name, size, age), Enter opens (`workspace::open_file`), actions Copy Image, Show in Finder (`workspace::reveal`), Copy Path, Move to Trash (destructive Confirm, `files::trash`, then delete the row; remove the files::trash dead_code expect if one is still present), rows whose file is gone are dropped on refresh. Verbs: `flick capture area|window` (async, reply `Select an area`), `flick capture screen|display <n>|rect <x,y,w,h> [--out <path>] [--no-copy]` (synchronous on the main thread, like rebuild version, bounded by the process exit), `flick capture ls [--limit n]`, `flick capture last`; with `cx.json` they answer `{"path":...,"width":...,"height":...,"copied":true}` or an array of those. `verbs()` = `capture area|window|screen|display|rect|ls|last`. Hotkeys: Binding keys `area`, `window`, `screen`. Characterization: `src/characterization/item_ids.rs` test `capture_ids_are_fixed_keys` (pins `capture:area`, `capture:window`, `capture:screen`, `capture:recent`, `capture:shot/<id>`), and a control_replies test that pins the `flick --json capture ls` shape on an empty store. Unit tests via `test_cx`: settings parsing and errors start with `[capture]: `, name template and collision suffix, store insert/list/cap/delete, command parsing (bad rect, unknown verb), result draining with a fake shot. Coverage floors: `src/modules/capture/name.rs` and `store.rs` at the measured value (target 100).

6. Wire annotation (needs 3, 4, 5). Items: `capture:area-annotate` Capture Area and Annotate (shot, then `ink::editor::edit(src = shot, dest = shot)`), `capture:draw` Draw on Screen / Stop Drawing on Screen (title from `overlay::drawing()`), `capture:cursor` Highlight Cursor / Stop Highlighting Cursor, `capture:clear` Clear Drawing (only while strokes exist). Recent view action Annotate: `dest` = `<stem> annotated.png` beside the source, recorded as a new row when `on_done(Saved|Copied)` posts ModuleChanged (the module keeps the pending dest and checks the file exists). Verbs: `flick capture area --annotate`, `flick capture draw on|off|toggle|clear`, `flick capture cursor on|off|toggle`, `flick capture annotate <path>`. Config `[capture]`: `colors = ["#ff3b30", "#ffcc00", "#34c759", "#0a84ff", "#ffffff"]` (hex parse errors start with `[capture]: `), `width = 4.0`, `fade_secs = 0.0`, `halo_color`, `halo_radius = 28.0`, hotkeys `annotate_hotkey`, `draw_hotkey`, `cursor_hotkey`. On `Event::DisplaysChanged`: `overlay::relayout()`. Delete the dead_code expects added in steps 2-4 (an unfulfilled expect fails the lint, which forces this). Add the new item ids to the characterization test from step 5.

7. Docs and smoke: README section Capture (items, verbs with --json, config, Screen Recording permission, where files go, how Trash works), ARCHITECTURE platform row (`capture`, `ink`, `pasteboard::set_png`), DEFAULT_CONFIG commented `[capture]` example in src/config.rs, and the manual checklist from acceptance.

alternatives.name: ScreenCaptureKit (SCScreenshotManager) as the backend, as the seed text says
alternatives.rejected_because: It returns through async completion handlers while control requests must answer synchronously on the main thread, it brings no selection UI (Flick would need its own crosshair, window picker and multi-display handling), and it adds objc2-screen-capture-kit and much more unsafe code. screencapture gives all of that today. Revisit when a feature needs live frames (scrolling capture, recording).

alternatives.name: CGWindowListCreateImage
alternatives.rejected_because: Deprecated and unavailable in the macOS 15+ SDK.

alternatives.name: Put the annotation model in src/core
alternatives.rejected_because: It is feature code used only by platform::ink and the capture module; core stays free of features (CLAUDE.md). It lives in platform as plain Rust with its own 100% coverage floor.

alternatives.name: Route canvas mouse events through the controller and the module (panel style)
alternatives.rejected_because: Drag events at display rate through events::post and the registry add latency and borrow contention for no gain; the module only needs results (a file, a done signal).

alternatives.name: Use platform::status_item as a drawing-mode indicator
alternatives.rejected_because: status_item manages one item that the activity module owns (flick-a513); visible strokes and the halo are the indicator.

alternatives.name: Store screenshots as blobs in flick.db
alternatives.rejected_because: Files are what users share and what Finder, Preview and agents read; the table only indexes paths.

risks: Parallelism: steps 1 and 2 touch disjoint files (platform/capture.rs + pasteboard.rs; platform/ink/model.rs). Step 5 needs only 1 and runs beside 3 and 4. Both 1 and 2 add a line to src/platform/mod.rs: trivial merge.

Screen Recording permission (TCC) is tied to the signed bundle and cannot be granted in the agent sandbox, so `capture::run` tests are #[ignore] and the real capture, the prompt and the editor are manual smokes. Do not run relaunch scripts from tests (mx-79796b).
macOS 15+ shows a periodic Screen Recording reconfirmation prompt for apps that capture; that is system behavior, document it.

screencapture behavior: exit code 0 with no file on Esc (treated as Cancelled); pin flags -i, -w, -R, -D, -C, -o, -x, -t in the args test and check `man screencapture` on the current OS during step 1.

Main thread: synchronous verbs (screen/display/rect) block the main thread for a few hundred ms; interactive verbs never block (worker thread + ModuleChanged). Never call capture::run with Target::Area or Window on the main thread.
files::trash may still carry a dead_code expect citing flick-4077; whichever of 4077 and step 5 lands first removes it.

Editor focus: Flick is an accessory app, so the editor must activate Flick; that emits AppActivated for Flick itself. Activity (flick-a513) ignores Flick's own pid. After the editor closes, the previous app should be re-activated.
Overlay must never steal focus or block clicks when not drawing: ignoresMouseEvents true outside draw mode, panels ordered out when empty; verify with the launcher panel open over the overlay.
Global NSEvent monitors for mouse events need no Accessibility permission, but key monitors would; the overlay takes keys only as the key window in draw mode.
Retina: screencapture writes pixels with 144 DPI metadata; the editor shows points and exports at pixel size. Mixed-DPI multi-display setups need a manual check.
File size cap 500 lines (mx-e7e3ab): keep ink split into model.rs, view.rs, editor.rs, overlay.rs and the module into mod.rs, store.rs, name.rs, run.rs (+ view.rs if needed).
Binary size: no new crates; check:binary-size must stay under 5 MB.
Table names must start with `capture` (mx-c65bc5). No cfg(test)-only expect attributes for unwrap/panic lints (mx-db1a9b, mx-7376a8).
ASSUMPTION: default save dir is ~/Pictures/Flick, copy and save on, shutter sound on.
ASSUMPTION: annotation is minimal: arrow, rectangle, pen, highlighter, text, solid redact box, 5 colors, undo/redo. Blur, crop, OCR, pin-to-screen, scrolling capture and recording are out of scope.
ASSUMPTION: capture is enabled by default and all hotkeys are unbound by default.
ASSUMPTION: deleting a shot from Recent moves the file to the Trash and drops the row; trimming history never touches files.
acceptance: `scripts/check-all.sh` passes after every step; src/core stays at 100%; src/platform/ink/model.rs at 100%; all unsafe/objc2 code only in src/platform (check:layers); release binary < 5 MB; no file over 500 lines.
The module is src/modules/capture/ plus one `modules!` line; capture imports no other module; its only table starts with `capture`.

Unit tests: screencapture args for every Target and flag; png_size on valid, truncated and non-PNG bytes; Canvas begin/drag/end/undo/redo/clear/expire, zero-size shapes dropped, arrow head geometry, key map; name template + collision suffix; store insert/list/cap/delete; command parsing and --json shapes; characterization pins capture item ids and the `flick --json capture ls` reply.
Manual: Capture Area from the launcher hides the panel, shows the native crosshair, and after a drag the PNG is in ~/Pictures/Flick and on the clipboard; Esc cancels with no file and no row.

Manual: Capture Window picks a window with shadow (no shadow with `shadow = false`); `flick --json capture screen | jq .ok.path` prints an existing file path; `flick capture rect 0,0,400,300 --no-copy` leaves the clipboard unchanged.

sections.context: Flick now records and serves my context: activity spans (src/modules/activity, `flick activity today|week|spans --json`), tasks (pl-3245: `flick task ls|report --json`, Event::TaskChanged), herdr agents on all machines (pl-49bb: `flick herdr ls|status --json`), screenshots (pl-5f0f: `flick capture screen --json` gives a path), and a live event stream (`flick events`). The control socket answers `flick <module> <verb>` with structured replies (Cx.json, core::control::split_json, Reply::answer). The epic: Flick is the sensor and the store, and an agent session (claude or pi, remote models acceptable per r-5f73/q-3570) is the copilot. Flick has no agent loop. The agent reads Flick's state only through the CLI. Activity data reaches it only with my explicit permission. That permission does not exist yet: pl-ac04 calls remote use out of scope, and the activity module has no permission code. So this plan defines it. Facts checked read-only: `claude` (~/.local/bin) supports -p, --output-format json (result, session_id, is_error, total_cost_usd), --append-system-prompt, --tools, --allowedTools/--disallowedTools, --session-id <uuid>, --resume, --add-dir, --model, --max-budget-usd. `pi` (~/.bun/bin) supports -p, --mode json, --append-system-prompt, --tools, --session-id, --session, @file attachments, --model, --provider. Neither binary nor `flick` is on the launchd PATH. `platform::notify::on_click` takes one handler, and the first one set wins (OnceLock). herdr (flick-adda) will hold it. herdr 0.9.1 has agent.start/agent.prompt, but those are writes, and this epic does not require herdr writes.
sections.approach:
Module `bridge` (src/modules/bridge/, registry line `mod bridge => "bridge", bridge::Bridge::default;` as the last line of `modules!`), plus one core/control/CLI flag and a permission in the activity module. The bridge imports no other module. It reaches them only through control verbs: it runs Flick's own binary (`std::env::current_exe()`) as a child process, `flick --remote ... --json`, from its worker thread. It reaches them through events: ModuleChanged for its own runs, and the brief tells an interactive agent about `flick events`. It reaches them through view names: Outcome::Push of its own views. No FFI in the module. Spawning, timeouts and process groups follow the rebuild pattern: `$SHELL -lc`, `process_group(0)`, `/bin/kill -TERM -- -pgid`. Seven steps.

1. Remote flag (src/core/control.rs, src/core/module.rs, src/control/mod.rs, src/app.rs, src/cli/mod.rs + client.rs, src/characterization/, ARCHITECTURE.md). New `core::control::REMOTE = "--remote"`. `split_flags(words) -> (Vec<String>, Flags { json: bool, remote: bool })` takes a trailing `--json` off first, then a trailing `--remote`; `split_json` becomes a thin wrapper or is replaced at its one caller. `Cx` gains `pub remote: bool`: the request came from a session that may send its output to a remote model. It is false for the launcher, events and hotkeys, and `test_cx` sets it false. `app::control(words, flags)` sets it. The CLI client appends `--remote` before `--json` when the env var `FLICK_REMOTE` is set and not empty; `flick events` ignores it. Modules that ignore `cx.remote` behave exactly as before. Tests: split_flags table (none, json, remote, both, `--json --remote` order, a lone `--remote` as a real argument in the middle stays), CLI parse with and without the env var (pass env in as a parameter, no global env mutation in tests), and a characterization test that pins the reply shapes for remote and non-remote requests. src/core stays at 100%. ARCHITECTURE Control socket section updated in the same commit.

2. Activity grant (src/modules/activity/remote.rs new, small edits to mod.rs). Stored in the existing `activity_state` key/value table, so no migration: `remote_until` (unix secs; 0 or missing = off; i64::MAX = always) and `remote_last` (time of the last remote read). Verbs: `flick activity remote allow [<minutes>|always]` (default 60), `remote deny`, `remote status` (`{"granted":bool,"until":..,"last_read":..}` with --json). With `cx.remote`, `allow`/`deny` always fail: an agent cannot grant itself. With `cx.remote` and no live grant, `today|week|spans` return Err("activity: remote use not permitted; the user can run `flick activity remote allow` or choose 'Allow Agents to Read Activity' in Flick"). `status` stays allowed. `on|off|forget` are always refused for remote callers. With a live grant, remote replies drop window titles unless `[activity] remote_titles = true` (default false), and each read updates `remote_last`. Root item `activity:remote` (permanent id): 'Allow Agents to Read Activity (1 h)' when off, 'Revoke Agent Activity Access · 42 min left' when on. Expiry is checked lazily on each call, with no timer. Tests with test_cx with remote true/false, a fixed clock (Env.now), expiry at the boundary, title stripping, and the self-grant refusal. Keep mod.rs under 500 lines.

3. Bridge pure core (src/modules/bridge/agent.rs, brief.rs, mod.rs with the module-level dead_code expect citing step 4; floors of 100.0 for both files in scripts/coverage-budgets.json). `Kind { Claude, Pi }`. `Launch { kind, exe, model, args, max_usd, allow: Vec<String>, cwd }`. `oneshot_argv(&Launch, brief, prompt, session, attach: Option<&Path>) -> Vec<String>`. For claude: `-p --output-format json --tools Bash[,Read] --allowedTools <Bash(flick <verb>:*) for each allow entry, plus the `flick --json <verb>` form> --disallowedTools Bash(flick bridge:*) Bash(flick activity remote:*) --append-system-prompt <brief> --session-id <uuid> [--model] [--max-budget-usd] [--add-dir <attach dir> + allowed Read(<attach>)] -- <prompt>`. For pi: `-p --mode json --tools bash[,read] --append-system-prompt <brief> --session-id <id> [--model] [@attach] -- <prompt>`. `interactive_argv` is the same without -p and the output format. `resume_argv(kind, exe, session)` gives `claude --resume <uuid>` or `pi --session <id>`. `shell_wrap(argv)` gives `[$SHELL, -lc, 'exec "$@"', flick-bridge, argv...]`, positional, so there is no quoting injection. `session_id(bytes: [u8;16]) -> String` gives a UUID v4 format; the bytes come from /dev/urandom in step 4. `parse_claude(stdout) -> Answer { text, session, cost_usd, error }` and `parse_pi(stdout)` read JSON lines (last assistant text, with a fallback to raw stdout trimmed to 64 KB). brief.rs: `brief(&BriefInput { now_local, allow, context: Vec<(String /*verb*/, Result<String,String>)>, interactive }) -> String`. The text covers: who the user is and that Flick is a local launcher that stores their context; the rule to read state only with `flick <module> <verb> --json` (with `--json` last); the allowed verbs; the rule that 'not permitted' means stop and tell the user how to grant, never work around it (never read flick.db or files under ~/Library/Application Support/Flick); no input to herdr agents; `flick events` for watching (interactive only); and the context snapshot, each verb's output clipped to 4 KB and 16 KB in total. Spike, done by hand once with tiny prompts (it costs cents): capture one `claude -p --output-format json` and one `pi -p --mode json` output, strip personal data, and commit them as fixtures under src/modules/bridge/fixtures/.

4. Module `bridge`, without UI (src/modules/bridge/mod.rs, config.rs, store.rs, run.rs, tests.rs). Config `[bridge]`: agent = "claude" (claude | pi), claude = "claude", pi = "pi" (resolved by the login shell), model = "", args = [], max_usd = 0.0 (0 = no cap), cwd = "" (empty = ~/Library/Caches/Flick/bridge, created 0700), context = ["task ls", "herdr ls", "activity today"], allow = ["task", "herdr ls", "herdr status", "activity today", "activity week", "activity status"], timeout_secs = 300, history = 50, notify = true, keyword = "ask", hotkey = "", terminal = ["wezterm", "start", "--cwd", "{cwd}", "--"]. Store migration 1: `bridge_runs(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, started INTEGER NOT NULL, finished INTEGER, agent TEXT NOT NULL, session TEXT NOT NULL, prompt TEXT NOT NULL, answer TEXT, status TEXT NOT NULL, error TEXT, cost REAL, attachment TEXT)`; `attachment` is here for step 6, so there is no second migration. Status is running, done, failed, cancelled or timeout. Rows beyond `history` are dropped. Started marks a leftover `running` row failed ('Flick quit during the run'). Runner (run.rs): at most one run at a time, on a named thread holding an Arc<Mutex<RunState>>. Order: (a) prefetch context, running `current_exe() --remote? ...`. In practice it runs the binary with env FLICK_REMOTE=1 and args `<verb words> --json`, a 5 s budget each, all in parallel; a failure becomes the Err text. (b) Build the brief and argv (step 3). (c) Spawn through `shell_wrap` with env FLICK_REMOTE=1, PATH = dir(current_exe) + inherited, HERDR_* removed, cwd as configured, stdin null, stdout/stderr captured, process_group(0). (d) Post Event::ModuleChanged { module: "bridge" } once a second while running. (e) Kill the group at timeout_secs or on cancel. (f) Parse, store, post ModuleChanged. Function pointers in an Env struct (now, spawn, exe) let tests use a fake agent script and a fake `flick` script in a temp dir, so no real claude/pi/flick runs in tests. CLI verbs (`verbs()`: `bridge ask|ls|show|cancel|open|brief|status|forget`): `ask [--agent claude|pi] <prompt...>` returns the run id at once (the main thread never waits on an agent); `ls [--json]`; `show <id> [--json]` (prompt, status, answer, session, cost); `cancel`; `open [<prompt...>]` runs the interactive session in the terminal argv with `{cwd}` filled, then `open -a` brings the terminal app to the front; `brief` prints the system prompt that would be sent (it runs the prefetch with a 5 s budget on the worker and returns 'brief: fetching, run again' until ready, or uses the last cached one); `status` (agent, exe resolution, running run, last error); `forget <id>|all --yes`. Every verb refuses when `cx.remote` (no recursion from an agent). `on_event`: Started settles; nothing else. Do not spawn in configure (it runs twice per reload, mx-56d580).

5. Launcher UI (src/modules/bridge/view.rs new; src/platform/notify.rs). Root items: 'Ask Agent…' (`bridge:ask`, opens form `bridge/ask` with Prompt (required) and Agent (default from config)), 'Open Agent Session' (`bridge:session`), and 'Agent Answers' (`bridge:runs`, subtitle 'running 0:42' or the last answer's first line). `direct`: a query starting with `<keyword> ` (default `ask `) gives 'Ask claude: <text>' at the top, and Enter starts the run, hides the launcher and shows status 'Asking claude…'. View `bridge/runs` (record_use = false): newest first; the running row shows elapsed time, refreshed by ModuleChanged; Enter pushes `bridge/answer` with the answer split into lines (read-only rows; Enter on a line copies it). Actions (cmd+K) on a run: Copy Answer, Continue in Terminal (resume_argv in the terminal argv), Cancel (while running), Delete (Confirm, not destructive). The hotkey opens `bridge/runs`. Notifications: when a run finishes and `notify = true`, `notify::post("bridge:<run id>", "<agent> answered", <first 120 chars of the answer>)`; the body holds no context data, only the answer. Platform change: add `notify::route(prefix: &'static str, handler: fn(&str))`. Clicks go to the first handler whose prefix matches the id, then to the `on_click` handler (herdr's), so the herdr call site does not change. Tests cover routing order, no match, and the unbundled no-op. A click on a bridge notification resumes that session in the terminal. The handler reads the terminal argv and executables from a module-level `static LAUNCH: Mutex<Option<Launch>>` that configure updates. Remove the notify dead_code expect if flick-adda has not already done so.

6. Screen context (src/modules/bridge/screen.rs new, small edits to view.rs/run.rs). 'Ask Agent About Screen…' (`bridge:screen`, form `bridge/ask-screen`) and `flick bridge ask --screen <prompt>`. The worker runs `current_exe() capture screen --no-copy --json` (without FLICK_REMOTE: the capture is a deliberate user action), parses `.path`, stores it in `attachment`, and passes it to the argv: claude gets the path in the prompt plus `--tools Bash,Read`, `--add-dir <dir>` and an allowed `Read(<path>)`; pi gets `--tools bash,read` and `@<path>`. The agent never gets `capture` in `allow` by default, so an agent cannot take screenshots itself. If capture is disabled or Screen Recording is denied, the run fails with capture's error text. The capture module owns the file; the bridge never deletes it.

7. Docs and smoke: README 'Agent bridge' section (what is sent where; remote models; FLICK_REMOTE and the activity grant; what the agent can and cannot run; where runs are stored; how to forget them), the activity section (remote grant, remote_titles), ARCHITECTURE (Cx.remote and the --remote word, the bridge's child-process pattern, notify routing), DEFAULT_CONFIG commented [bridge] example and `remote_titles`; run the manual checklist in acceptance.

Parallelism: steps 1 and 3 start together. Step 2 needs 1 and runs beside 3 and 4. Step 4 needs 1 and 3. Steps 5 and 6 need 4 and run in parallel. Step 7 is last.

alternatives.name: Bridge collects context by importing the task/activity/herdr modules or calling Registry from inside the module
alternatives.rejected_because: Breaks modules-are-independent (scripts/layer-rules.toml). The control verbs (`flick <module> <verb> --json`) are already the stable public API, and running them as a child process uses the same permission gate the agent faces.

alternatives.name: Agent loop inside Flick (Flick calls a model API, owns tools and conversation)
alternatives.rejected_because: The epic says no agent loop in Flick. It would also add an HTTP/TLS stack (binary budget < 5 MB) and a chat UI (r-5052 rejects chat UIs). claude and pi already own the loop, tools, sessions and auth.

alternatives.name: MCP server in Flick exposing state as tools
alternatives.rejected_because: More protocol surface (stdio JSON-RPC, schemas) for the same data the CLI already returns as JSON; both claude and pi run shell commands well. Revisit if a second, non-shell client appears.

alternatives.name: Spawn interactive sessions in a herdr pane via `herdr agent start` / `agent.prompt`
alternatives.rejected_because: Those are herdr writes. The herdr module is read-only and this epic does not require writes. A WezTerm window needs no herdr changes. A later seed can add a herdr launch target with its own confirm step.

alternatives.name: Identify agent callers by a separate agent-only control socket
alternatives.rejected_because: Needs a second listener and socket lifecycle in src/control. A trailing `--remote` word set from an env var mirrors the existing `--json` contract with about 50 lines. Neither stops a determined agent with a shell, so the cheaper one wins (see risks).

alternatives.name: Event-triggered runs ([[bridge.trigger]] on task_changed / herdr blocked)
alternatives.rejected_because: That is an always-on loop, and r-5f73 calls it far down the line. It costs model calls without a user action. v1 runs only when asked; an interactive session can watch `flick events` itself.

alternatives.name: Per-module remote gates everywhere (task, herdr, capture) in this epic
alternatives.rejected_because: The epic requires the gate only for activity data. Tasks and herdr status are low-sensitivity and allowlisted per verb. Screenshots are sent only on an explicit per-use action. `Cx.remote` makes adding more gates later a local change in each module.

risks: Epic note says 'far-future stretch; do not design yet'. Plan submitted parked at priority 4; building waits for user go-ahead because runs send context to remote models and cost money. The step-3 fixture spike calls real claude/pi and must be run by the user, never by an agent.

Cross-plan dependencies (add with `sd dep add` after submit): step 2 needs flick-a30b and flick-86be (both edit activity mod.rs/report.rs); step 5 needs flick-adda (notify wired, dead_code expect gone); step 6 needs flick-e24c (`capture screen --json` path); step 7 needs flick-feab, flick-6d92 (default context verbs exist) and flick-d212 (README Activity section).

The permission is a guard against accidents, not against a hostile agent: FLICK_REMOTE is an env var and the gate is a request word. A pi session with bash, or an interactive claude session where I approve commands, can run `env -u FLICK_REMOTE flick activity spans` or read flick.db. Mitigation: claude one-shots get only `--tools Bash` with a per-verb allowlist, so other commands are denied in -p mode; the brief forbids workarounds; the default agent is claude. Document it plainly in the README.

Privacy: context and answers leave the machine (remote models, accepted for the bridge in r-5f73/q-3570). Activity data is sent only with a live grant, and without titles unless remote_titles = true. herdr previews in `herdr ls` (other agents' output) and task titles go to the model when listed in `context`/`allow`. Screenshots go only on an explicit per-use action. Notifications show only the answer's first line. Runs are stored locally (bridge_runs, capped at `history`), and `bridge forget` deletes them.

Self-escalation: an agent must not grant itself access or spawn more agents. Mitigation: `activity remote allow|deny` and every `bridge` verb refuse when cx.remote, and the claude argv also disallows `Bash(flick bridge:*)` and `Bash(flick activity remote:*)`. Unit tests pin all of these.

Main thread: control requests run on the main thread, so a verb must never wait on an agent or on the prefetch (which calls back into the same socket and would deadlock). `ask` returns a run id; prefetch and spawn run only on the bridge worker thread. A test asserts that `command` does not join the worker.

PATH and auth under launchd: claude/pi/wezterm live in ~/.local/bin, ~/.bun/bin and /opt/homebrew/bin. The `$SHELL -lc 'exec "$@"'` wrapper loads the user's PATH and API-key env; dir(current_exe) is prepended so the agent finds `flick`. `bridge status` reports what the login shell resolves (bounded to 2 s).
Output format drift (claude --output-format json, pi --mode json): parsers ignore unknown fields and fall back to raw stdout trimmed to 64 KB; fixtures come from a real spike in step 3.
Cost and runaway runs: one run at a time, timeout_secs = 300 kills the process group, optional max_usd passes --max-budget-usd to claude, and cost is shown in `bridge show`.

Notification clicks: platform::notify keeps one on_click handler (herdr). The new prefix routing must not change herdr's behaviour; tests pin that ids without a registered prefix still reach on_click. The bundle-id no-op (mx-f5bdcc) still applies under cargo run and tests.

Tests must never run the real claude, pi, wezterm, `open` or the real Flick socket. Use the Env fn-pointer pattern, fake agent and fake `flick` shell scripts in per-test temp dirs (mx-231c5f: no shared temp dir), and short /tmp paths if a socket is needed (mx-6c21fe).

Gates: files stay under 500 lines (bridge split into mod.rs, config.rs, store.rs, run.rs, view.rs, screen.rs, agent.rs, brief.rs, tests.rs; activity's grant in remote.rs); src/core at 100% after step 1; floors of 100.0 for bridge/agent.rs and bridge/brief.rs; no new crates (UUIDs from /dev/urandom), binary < 5 MB; the dead_code expect in step 3 is removed in step 4 (mx-264628: removing it exposes every unused item); table names start with `bridge` (mx-c65bc5); no cfg(test)-only expect for unwrap/panic lints (mx-db1a9b, mx-7376a8); new root items may need the modules::tests reload fix (mx-cd1f4d).

Terminal launch differs by terminal: `wezterm start` may open in a running GUI instance or a new process. The terminal argv is configurable (`{cwd}` placeholder), and the manual smoke checks WezTerm with and without a running instance.
